F3.basis: Canonical judgment-and-decision-making construct; names the field the column sits in.

F5.basis: Lee & See, Human Factors 46(1) 2004, 'Trust in Automation: Designing for Appropriate Reliance', doi:10.1518/hfes.46.1.50_30392; Schemmer et al., IUI 2023, doi:10.1145/3581641.3584066. States the target rather than the failure, as the other columns do.

F9.basis: Attested in the column's own 218 papers: guid* in 72, feedback in 52, critique in only 5. One term per sub-factor - guidance for 'direction while stuck' (176), feedback for 'external critique' (54).

F11.basis: Nass & Moon, J. Soc. Issues 56(1) 2000, 'Machines and Mindlessness', doi:10.1111/0022-4537.00153; Davis 1989 (TAM). Its one sub-factor is 'acceptance and social perception of the agent'.

F13.basis: Kept as Personalization at the PI's direction. Note for the record: its sub-factors are engagement and immersion (291), motivation (94), behaviour change (56) and long-term adherence (46) - personalization is the remedy those papers apply, not the factor itself.

F16.basis: Edmondson, ASQ 44(2) 1999, doi:10.2307/2666999 (psychological safety); Malone & Crowston, ACM Comput. Surv. 1994 (coordination). Names both halves: coordination (73), minority voice and psychological safety (24), consensus (21).

F19.basis: Shortened from 'Effort, cognitive load and attention' for parallel structure; attention survives as a sub-factor (91).

F20.basis: Bandura 1977 (self-efficacy). Shortened from 'Skill, expertise and self-efficacy'; the expertise barrier survives as a sub-factor (385).

F21.basis: 184 of its papers are social sharing and human connection (128) and social presence and team rapport (56) - relational, not only emotional.

F22.basis: Unchanged in substance; Title Case for parallel structure.

pattern_sort.distinctive_breadth: factors the pattern reaches at >= 1.25x the corpus base rate, minimum 5 papers
pattern_sort.effective_breadth: exp(Shannon entropy) over the pattern's factor distribution
pattern_sort.why_not_raw_breadth: 35 of 83 patterns touch all 21 factors and 61 touch 19 or more; a raw distinct count is almost all ties.
